title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is the closed annulus U x J, with U the unit circle and J = [-1,1]. Points are written (z,s), and the two boundary circles are s = -1 and s = +1. The universal cover is X~ = R x J, with z = exp(2 i pi t).

On the previous page Grothendieck took the group of 'shears' f_{a,theta}(z,s) = (z theta exp(2 i pi a s), s). He kept those whose restriction to each boundary circle is a rotation of finite order, which forces a in Q and theta in mu_inf. Adding the finite symmetries mu x mu (mu = {+1,-1}) gives
- G = (mu x mu) semidirect (Q x mu_inf), and
- its lift G~ = (mu x mu) semidirect (Q x Q),
- with an exact sequence 1 -> Z -> G~ -> G -> 1, where b in Q maps to theta = exp(2 i pi b).

This page writes the actions explicitly.

(32) On the cover: ((e,e').f_{a,b})(t,s) = (e'(t + a s + b), e e' s), with e, e' in mu, a, b in Q, t in R, s in J.

(33) Passing to the quotient by Z gives the action on X: ((e,e').g_{a,theta})(z,s) = ((z theta exp(2 i pi a s))^{e'}, e e' s), with theta in mu_inf.

Interpretation of the signs:
- The linear part (t,s) -> (e't, e e' s) has determinant e, so e is the orientation character.
- e e' records whether the two boundary components ('the set of holes', pi_0(dX)) are swapped.
- e' records composition with complex conjugation.
- On dX the element acts by the two rotations theta exp(-2 i pi a) (at s = -1) and theta exp(+2 i pi a) (at s = +1), followed by the swap and/or conjugation.

A crossed-out computation, (34)-(35), solves for both boundary rotations equal to -1. This gives two families: theta = 1 with a in 1/2 + Z, or theta = -1 with a in Z.

The next page restricts to G_0 (theta = 1). There g_a(z,s) = (z exp(2 i pi a s), s) is the identity on dX iff a is in Z, i.e. iff g_a is an honest power of the Dehn twist.

Purpose: this is a careful bookkeeping of the 'rational' (fractional) Dehn twists of the annulus, extended by orientation and swap symmetries. It is groundwork for the role of cylinders and their twist groups in the Teichmüller tower and Lego (pants and cylinder decompositions) programme of the 'Teichmülleries'.
errors: The prose lists the two boundary rotations as 'theta exp(2i pi a), theta exp(2i pi a)'. The first should be theta exp(-2i pi a), for the component s = -1, as in the previous page and the crossed-out (34). This is a slip of the pen.

Otherwise the formulas check. In particular, conjugating the shear (t,s) -> (t + as + b, s) by (t,s) -> (e't, e e' s) gives a -> e a and b -> e' b. This confirms the semidirect product structure 'by symmetry on the two factors'. The crossed-out solutions (35) are also correct.

ideas.what: The group of rational shears / fractional twists of the annulus, extended by orientation reversal, boundary swap and conjugation, and lifted to the universal cover with kernel Z (the integral Dehn twists).
ideas.modern_name: fractional (rational) Dehn twists of the annulus; mapping class / isometry group of a cylinder modulo full twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn twists: Dehn/Lickorish. Fractional Dehn twist coefficients: Gabai–Oertel, Honda–Kazez–Matić (2000s), in a different setting.
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses Lego / Teichmüller tower building blocks informally; these explicit formulas do not appear there as far as known.

ideas.what: Decoding the signs (e, e') as orientation character, action on pi_0 of the boundary, and complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: action of a dihedral-type extension on boundary components; orientation character

missed.claim: Grothendieck works with the group Q of rational twists on the annulus. Its finite-order boundary rotations and its integral subgroup Z are exactly the full twists. This loosely prefigures later uses of rational/fractional twist parameters, such as fractional Dehn twist coefficients and rational twists in tangential base point / Teichmüller tower settings. The page itself is elementary bookkeeping, though.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of minor historical interest only. It documents that Grothendieck considered Q-twists, with roots-of-unity boundary rotations, as symmetries of the cylinder building block. The mathematics is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: These are explicit, correct but elementary formulas for a group of symmetries of the annulus, with a crossed-out sign computation. It is routine bookkeeping within the Teichmüller notes.
transcription_corrections: In the prose, the two rotations are written identically in the manuscript ('θ exp(2iπa), θ exp(2iπa)'). The intended values are θ exp(-2iπa) and θ exp(2iπa).
Under (32) the manuscript annotates ε, ε' ∈ μ, a, b ∈ ℚ, t ∈ ℝ, s ∈ J by arrows. Under (33) it annotates ε, ε' ∈ μ, a ∈ ℚ, θ ∈ μ_∞.
The margin deletion near (32) reads roughly 'x = ε(t, εε's)'. The whole block (34)-(35) at the bottom is crossed out.
